gloss.intro: The words developers (and the AI teams) use, in plain English.
gloss.switch.help: Dotted words get a plain explanation when you hover them.
gloss.backlog.text: Ideas and work not planned in yet. Nothing there gets worked on until it moves to To do.
gloss.sprint.text: A short stretch of work (often a week or two) with an agreed set of cards to finish.
gloss.standup.text: A quick check-in: what each team member did, what they do next, and what is stopping them.
gloss.bug.text: Something that doesn’t work the way it should.
gloss.test.text: Trying a finished piece of work to check it does what was asked, before you accept it.
gloss.commit.text: A saved snapshot of the code, with a short note of what changed. You can always go back to one.
gloss.push.text: Sending saved snapshots (commits) from this computer up to GitHub, so they are backed up and shared.
gloss.branch.text: A separate line of work in the code, so changes can be made without touching the main version.
gloss.merge.text: Joining a branch’s changes back into the main version.
gloss.repo.text: The project’s folder of code and its full history of commits, usually also kept on GitHub.
gloss.refactor.text: Tidying the code without changing what it does: smaller files, clearer names, less repetition.
gloss.deploy.text: Putting a new version live, for example onto a server where people use it.
gloss.kanban.text: A board with columns (To do, In progress, Done) where cards move left to right as work happens.
gloss.wip.text: Work in progress: the most cards a column should hold, so the team finishes things before starting more.
gloss.pr.text: Asking for a branch’s changes to be checked and merged into the main version.
gloss.hook.text: A small command that runs by itself at a set moment, e.g. when an AI session starts, so the team hears your comments.
gloss.token.text: The unit AI usage is counted in: roughly a few letters of text read or written. Fewer tokens, more of your plan left.
gloss.agent.text: An AI that works on its own on a task: reads the code, makes changes, runs checks, and reports back.
gloss.title: 📖 Words explained
gloss.about: The words you meet in AI-gile, in plain language: building it, changing it safely, keeping it running for the people who use it, and working as a team with AI.
gloss.about.noai: The words you meet in AI-gile, in plain language: building it, changing it safely, keeping it running for the people who use it, and working as a team.
gloss.g.team: 🤝 Working as a team (and with AI)
gloss.qa.text: Short for quality assurance: the automatic checks that run before anything goes live. When QA is red, something failed, and it can’t go live until that is fixed.
gloss.release.text: A named bundle of finished work that goes live together, with short notes on what changed. 🚀 Releases writes the notes from the done cards.
gloss.rollback.text: Going back to the last version that worked when a new one causes trouble. In AI-gile it makes a checklist of the undo steps written on each change.
gloss.live.text: The real version that people use, as opposed to a copy for trying things out. Developers also call it production.
gloss.change.text: A planned change to something people rely on, written down first: what, why, the risk, when, and how to undo it. Start one with 🔀 Raise a change.
gloss.risk.text: Something that could go wrong, scored on how likely and how bad it would be. ⚠️ Risks keeps them in one list, highest score first, each with a date to look again.
gloss.chgwin.text: The times when changes may go live, such as a quiet Tuesday evening. Outside a window a change card can’t be finished, unless it is an emergency.
gloss.gonogo.text: A quick vote just before a change goes live: each person who has to approve says Go or No go. It only goes ahead when they agree.
gloss.approval.text: Waiting for a yes before work starts. A card a friend raises, or a change, waits in ✅ Approvals until you approve or decline it.
gloss.quiettime.text: A stretch of time, like a stream, a demo or the night, when nothing goes live. The teams keep working and testing, but going live waits until it ends. Elsewhere it is called a change freeze.
gloss.service.text: Something you built that people rely on, like a website or an app, looked after so it keeps working. Tick “This project is a service” and say what it offers, who uses it and who is on call.
gloss.uptime.text: An automatic check, every few minutes, that your service still answers. If it fails several times in a row, AI-gile opens an incident card by itself.
gloss.statuspage.text: A public page that shows whether a service is working (green, orange or red) with the latest update, so the people who use it can check instead of asking.
gloss.incident.text: Something that is broken for the people using it right now, like the website being down. A 🔥 incident card jumps the queue: getting it working again comes first.
gloss.major.text: A big incident: many people affected, or money or data at risk. One button puts every team on it (swarm), wakes whoever is on call and asks for a status update every 30 minutes.
gloss.oncall.text: Being the one who answers when something breaks, even at night. Each service has an on-call team member who is woken first for its incidents.
gloss.replyby.text: How long a card may wait for a first answer, for example an hour for an incident. After that it gets a red clock, so nothing is quietly forgotten. Also called a response target.
gloss.postmortem.text: A short look back after an incident: what happened, what helped and what to change, without blaming anyone. An incident can’t be closed without one.
gloss.problem.text: The hidden cause behind one or more incidents. A 🧩 problem card groups incidents that keep coming back, so the cause is found and fixed for good.
gloss.rootcause.text: The real reason something broke, not just what you saw going wrong. Fix the root cause and the incident stops coming back.
gloss.workaround.text: A way to keep things working until the real fix is ready, like restarting something when it gets stuck. It is written on the problem card so nobody has to work it out again.
gloss.knownerror.text: A problem whose cause is understood and that has a workaround, but isn’t fixed yet. 🧩 Known errors lists them, so everyone uses the workaround instead of digging again.
gloss.runbook.text: Step-by-step instructions for fixing a known kind of trouble, so it is done the same way, quickly, every time. After a big incident the team can propose one for you to OK.
gloss.backup.text: A saved copy of your data from earlier, to fall back on if something is lost or damaged. AI-gile makes a backup of your boards every day.
gloss.restore.text: Putting data back from a backup. A backup only really counts once you know it can be restored, so it is worth trying now and then.
gloss.ci.text: One thing your service depends on, like a server, a domain, a certificate, a key or a supplier. 🗂️ Configuration items lists them per service, so you can see what an incident affects and what needs renewing or a backup.
gloss.expiry.text: AI-gile keeps an eye on dates like when a certificate or a domain runs out. Within 30 days of the date it makes one card to renew it, so nothing stops working by surprise.
gloss.desk.text: Where questions and reports from the people using your service come in. AI-gile sorts each one into a request, an incident or an idea, and says so when it looks like something already reported.
gloss.svcrequest.text: Someone asking for something ordinary, like a new account or a bit of help, rather than reporting that something is broken. It waits its turn; an incident goes first.
gloss.svcreview.text: A look back at one month of a service: incidents opened and fixed, how quickly people got an answer, uptime and tokens used. The Monthly review shows it for each service.
gloss.accessreview.text: Checking every 90 days who can still get in: share links, friends’ roles and kept secrets. You keep or remove each one, so old access doesn’t linger.
gloss.improvements.text: Everything the team decided to get better at, in one place: retro suggestions, review actions and problem fixes, each with its status. Find it under 📈 Improvements.
gloss.tokencap.text: A monthly limit on the tokens a service’s agents may use. At 80% you get a warning; at 100% their background work waits until next month or until you raise the cap.
gloss.dod.text: The team’s short checklist of what “finished” means, like tested and explained, before a card is handed to you. Its twin, the Definition of Ready, says when a card is clear enough to start.
gloss.testpile.text: The finished cards waiting for you to try, one after another. Accept one or send it back with a note, and the next one comes up.
gloss.retro.text: A look back at how the team works, to agree on one thing to do better. In AI-gile a retro suggests a change to the team’s ways of working, and you say Go or Not yet.
gloss.peerreview.text: A second pair of eyes: another AI checks each card’s work before it reaches you, so fewer mistakes get through.
gloss.swarm.text: All hands on deck: every team drops other work to help on one urgent project until it is sorted. Other projects wait meanwhile.
gloss.scrummaster.text: The one who keeps the work flowing: spots stuck cards, nudges the teams and reminds you of what is waiting. In AI-gile the Lead Scrum Master does this across every project.
gloss.scrummaster.text.noai: The one who keeps the work flowing: spots stuck cards and reminds you of what is waiting. Without AI it works with fixed commands, like sorting To do.
